question: Which architectural style is the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Tamil Nadu known for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Brihadeeswarar Temple**, located in **Thanjavur**, **Tamil Nadu**, is one of the most celebrated examples of **Dravidian Architecture**. This style is characterized by its pyramid-shaped towers, known as **Vimanas**, and large temple complexes. **Dravidian** architecture is the correct answer because the temple exhibits all the classic features of this South Indian style, such as the **Vimana**, **Mandapa**, and **Gopurams**.

• The temple was built by the **Chola Emperor Raja Raja Chola I** between **1003 AD** and **1010 AD**. It was a symbol of the **Chola Dynasty's** power and their devotion to **Lord Shiva**.

• A unique feature of this temple is its **Vimana** (the tower over the sanctum), which stands at a height of **216 feet** (approximately **66 meters**). At the time of its construction, it was one of the tallest structures in the world.

• The temple is constructed entirely out of **granite**. This is a remarkable feat because there are no granite sources within a **60-kilometer** radius of **Thanjavur**, implying a massive logistical effort during the **11th century**.

• The temple is part of the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** known as the **Great Living Chola Temples**, which also includes the **Brihadisvara Temple** at **Gangaikonda Cholapuram** and the **Airavatesvara Temple** at **Darasuram**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Nagara Style**: This architectural style is predominant in **Northern India**. Unlike the **Dravidian** style, the **Nagara** style features a beehive-shaped tower called a **Shikhara**. It typically does not have the massive **Gopurams** (gateways) or the large water tanks that are common in South Indian temples. Examples include the **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in **Khajuraho** and the **Sun Temple** in **Konark**.

• **Vesara Style**: This is a hybrid style that combines elements of both **Nagara** and **Dravidian** architecture. It flourished in the **Deccan** region of India, particularly under the **Chalukya** and **Hoysala** dynasties. The **Chennakesava Temple** at **Belur** is a famous example of this style.

• **Indo-Saracenic Style**: This is a **revivalist** architectural style used by **British architects** in India during the late **19th century**. It blends **Indo-Islamic**, **Hindu**, and **Gothic** elements. Notable examples include the **Victoria Memorial** in **Kolkata** and the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** in **Mumbai**.

• **Chola Art and Culture**: The **Chola** period is known as the **Golden Age** of **Tamil** culture. Apart from architecture, the **Cholas** were famous for their **bronze sculptures**, particularly the **Nataraja** (the dancing Shiva), and their extensive maritime trade across **Southeast Asia**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Kumbam** (the apex or the bulbous structure at the top of the tower) of the **Brihadeeswarar Temple** is carved out of a **single rock** and is estimated to weigh about **80 tons**.

• The temple is also known as **Dakshina Meru** (the Meru of the South). The **Shiva Linga** inside the sanctum is one of the largest in India, standing **3.7 meters** tall.

• The temple complex features a massive statue of **Nandi** (the sacred bull), which is also carved from a **single stone**. It measures about **13 feet** in height and **16 feet** in length.

• The walls of the temple are covered with **Chola-era frescoes** and **inscriptions** in **Tamil** and **Sanskrit**, which provide valuable historical data about the **Chola** administration, social life, and economy.

• In **2010**, the temple celebrated its **1000th anniversary**, an event marked by significant cultural celebrations and the release of a commemorative **1000-rupee coin** by the **Reserve Bank of India**.
